title: Centripetal force at B
description: Essential: The final answer for part (1) must be correctly stated as 7mg.

title: Displacement magnitude and direction
description: Essential: The final answer for part (2) must correctly give the magnitude as 2√2 R and the direction as 45° downward-left.

title: Spring work value
description: Essential: The final answer for part (3) must correctly state the work done by the spring as 5mgR.

title: Applying Newton's second law at B
description: Important: The student must correctly relate the given normal force (8mg) to the centripetal force using F_centripetal = N - mg.

title: Energy conservation with friction
description: Important: The work-energy theorem from A to B must be applied, accounting for spring work, kinetic energy at B, and work done by friction (μ=0.5 over distance 3R).

title: Projectile motion analysis
description: Important: After point C, the motion must be treated as projectile motion, correctly calculating horizontal and vertical displacements using v_C = √(gR).

title: Vector displacement composition
description: Optional: The total displacement after C should be found by combining horizontal and vertical components via the Pythagorean theorem and arctan.

title: Sign error in normal force
description: Pitfall: Incorrectly using F_centripetal = N + mg at point B, leading to an answer of 9mg.

title: Omitting friction work
description: Pitfall: Failing to subtract the work done by friction (1.5mgR) in the work-energy calculation for the spring.

title: Unit or direction omission
description: Pitfall: Stating the displacement magnitude without the required direction (45° downward-left) or omitting units/radicals.
